Solution to the exercise in [Lecture 11](../slides/lecture11.pdf).

## Minimizer and sampled gradient

Differentiating the average loss gives
$$
  H_N'(\theta) = \frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^N (\theta - y_i) = \theta - \bar{y}.
$$
Thus the minimizer is $\theta^* = \bar{y}$. If we sample observation $i$, its
gradient is $\theta - y_i$, and the SGD update is
$$
  \theta_{k+1} = \theta_k - \gamma_k(\theta_k - y_{I_k}).
$$

## Implementation

We use the same sampled indices for both learning rates so that the comparison
depends only on the rates.

```{r}
#| label: sgd-mean-solution

set.seed(1)

N <- 100
y <- rnorm(N, mean = 2)
steps <- 200
indices <- sample.int(N, steps, replace = TRUE)

run_sgd <- function(learning_rate) {
  theta <- numeric(steps + 1)

  for (k in seq_len(steps)) {
    i <- indices[k]
    gamma <- learning_rate(k)
    theta[k + 1] <- theta[k] - gamma * (theta[k] - y[i])
  }

  theta
}

constant <- run_sgd(function(k) 0.1)
decaying <- run_sgd(function(k) 1 / k)

plot(
  0:steps,
  constant,
  type = "l",
  col = "darkorange",
  ylim = range(constant, decaying, mean(y)),
  xlab = "Update",
  ylab = expression(theta[k])
)
lines(0:steps, decaying, col = "royalblue")
abline(h = mean(y), lty = 2)
legend(
  "bottomright",
  legend = c(
    "Fixed rate: 0.1",
    "Decaying rate: 1/k",
    "Sample mean"
  ),
  col = c("darkorange", "royalblue", "black"),
  lty = c(1, 1, 2),
  bty = "n"
)
```

The fixed rate keeps responding to each new observation, so its path continues
to fluctuate around $\bar{y}$. With $\gamma_k = 1/k$, the update produces the
running mean of the sampled observations. Its fluctuations shrink as more
observations are drawn, and it converges to $\bar{y}$.
